beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — convergent receptor topology
beats.narration_text: Targeted therapies block specific receptors. The assumption is that blocking the receptor blocks the signal. But cells have multiple receptor inputs that converge on the same hub — block one, and a second receptor activates and routes to the same node.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — topology diagram: two receptors, one hub, one output; block on receptor A; receptor B reroutes to hub; output unchanged; caption: convergence means upstream blocks don't stop the output

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — bypass resistance textbook case
beats.narration_text: MET amplification in EGFR-mutant lung cancer is the textbook case. Erlotinib blocks EGFR — receptor A — but the tumor amplifies MET — receptor B — which signals through the same downstream hub. The output, proliferation, is restored. Bypass resistance requires combination therapy hitting multiple inputs.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — EGFR/MET bypass diagram; erlotinib block on EGFR; MET arrow active to same hub; proliferation output restored; caption: bypass resistance — why one drug is never enough

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_BypassTrack class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The hub is a RoundedRectangle at the origin — GRAY, one point seven by one point seven. Receptor A is BLUE at upper-left; its arrow gets a VERM plug block and an X-mark built from two crossing lines. Receptor B starts at opacity zero point two and fades to full — the drug doesn't suppress it, so it activates. The output cluster is six GREEN circles in a three-by-two grid. The choreography: block A, reveal B, grow the B-to-hub arrow, Flash the output.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_BypassTrack
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; ORANGE="#E69F00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_BypassTrack(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    hub=RoundedRectangle(width=1.7,height=1.7,
      corner_radius=0.22,color=GRAY,
      fill_color=GRAY,fill_opacity=0.18,
      stroke_width=3.2).move_to(ORIGIN)
    recA=RoundedRectangle(width=1.9,height=1.1,
      corner_radius=0.18,color=BLUE,
      fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.16,
      stroke_width=3).move_to([-4.5,2.0,0])
    recB=RoundedRectangle(width=1.9,height=1.1,
      corner_radius=0.18,color=ORANGE,
      fill_color=ORANGE,fill_opacity=0.16,
      stroke_width=3).set_opacity(0.2).move_to([-4.5,-2.0,0])
    arrowA=Arrow([-3.55,1.8,0],[-0.85,0.5,0],color=GRAY)
    plug=Rectangle(width=0.3,height=0.7,
      color=VERM,fill_color=VERM,
      fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([-2.1,1.1,0])
    xmark=VGroup(
      Line([-2.3,1.3,0],[-1.9,0.9,0],color=VERM,stroke_width=6),
      Line([-2.3,0.9,0],[-1.9,1.3,0],color=VERM,stroke_width=6))
    out=VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.22,color=GREEN,
      fill_color=GREEN,fill_opacity=0.82)
      for _ in range(6)]).arrange_in_grid(2,3,buff=0.1)
    out.move_to([4.5,0,0])
    hubArrow=Arrow([0.85,0,0],[3.2,0,0],color=GRAY)
    arrowB=Arrow([-3.55,-1.8,0],[-0.85,-0.5,0],color=ORANGE)
    self.play(FadeIn(hub),FadeIn(recA),GrowArrow(arrowA))
    self.play(FadeIn(plug),FadeIn(xmark))
    self.play(recB.animate.set_opacity(1.0),GrowArrow(arrowB))
    self.play(GrowArrow(hubArrow))
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(c) for c in out],lag_ratio=0.12))
    self.wait(0.8)

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_BypassTrack — watch the block then the bypass
beats.narration_text: Run it. Hub and receptor A appear. The A-to-hub arrow grows. Then the VERM block slides onto the arrow and the X-mark appears. Receptor B fades from faint to full — it was there the whole time, just not activated. The B-to-hub arrow grows in ORANGE. The hub-to-output arrow grows. Six GREEN circles flash in. The output is identical whether A is blocked or not — that is the topology.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: animate signal flow as a dot. An ORANGE dot travels from receptor B along the B-arrow into the hub. A GRAY dot travels from the hub to the output cluster. Output circles assemble one at a time — LaggedStart. Then Flash the block on A's arrow at the end as a reminder: A is still blocked, B routed around it.

beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_BypassTrackFlow — dot animation + one-by-one output assembly
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. The block is in place on A. Receptor B activates. An ORANGE dot travels from B through the B-arrow into the hub. A GRAY dot leaves the hub and arrives at the output cluster. The six output circles appear one by one. Then the block on A's arrow Flashes — VERM, vermillion — to remind you: A is still dead. B routed around it. The output doesn't know. The tumor doesn't care.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: Same hub, different front door. The animation showed the critical topology: convergence means blocking upstream doesn't block the outcome if any other input feeds the same node. Claude ported the plate geometry in one prompt and added the dot-flow signal animation in one revision. The pattern — convergent receptors, one hub, animated dot as signal — works for any bypass resistance mechanism.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a third receptor to the hub — call it receptor C, in GREEN — and show it being blocked simultaneously with receptor A, leaving only receptor B as the active input. Why run it? Because combination therapy is exactly this: dual-blockade of two convergent inputs, leaving only the rarest bypass route open. Animating three inputs shows the student why two drugs are not just two drugs — they are a topological constraint on which routes to the hub remain viable. If the hub itself is druggable, that fourth option closes the last door.

with VERM plugs simultaneously, leaving only B active.
Animate: A and C blocked together, B signal flows to hub, output activates.
This models dual-blockade leaving one bypass route."
